subject: Prod inference audit — 1M-token unit economics & planned bench runs
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@cloudapps.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Prod inference audit — 1M-token unit economics & planned bench runs

Sam — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. I attached a short unit-econ workbook (redwood_unit_econ_v1.xlsx) that drives the numbers below.

Top-level takeaways from the discovery call:
- Primary workload: multi-turn chat assistant (~1.2k avg tokens/session, 3–6 calls per session).
- SLO: P95 latency <= 250ms for our recommended model stack; peak QPS ~ 160 req/s across geo.
- Current hyperscaler setup: batch-size=1 serving, CPU fallbacks for spikes; estimated spend from CloudApps dev team ~ $0.45 / 1k input tokens (rough).

Preliminary unit economics (apples-to-apples per 1M input+output tokens):
- Redwood (recommended config: fp16 quantized variant, batching 8, cache warm): ~$28–$34 per 1M tokens (assumes 60% KV cache hit on common prompts, GPU pooling with continuous batching).
- Hyperscaler managed endpoint (your cited config): ~$65–$80 per 1M tokens (batching=1, managed autoscaling, higher per-invocation overhead).

Key assumptions (please validate):
- Model: open Llama-family 33B equivalent runtime profile (we can swap to model you prefer).
- Cache hit: baseline 60% (we recommended measuring at 30/60/80% to see delta).
- Batching: Redwood continuous batching + small latency SLO keeps effective batch=6–10 on busy tails.
- Quantization: BF16->FP16 path; additional QAT/4-bit would further reduce costs if accuracy tolerates it.

Proposed test plan (minimal set to demonstrate delta):
1) Baseline throughput/latency run (both Redwood hosted and your hyperscaler staging): same model binary, same prompt mix, no KV cache. Measure cost per 1M tokens and P50/P95/P99 latencies. Owner: CloudApps + Redwood SMEs. Estimated 3 hours.
2) Cache effectiveness run: same workload with KV/prefix cache enabled; measure hit-rate and cost delta at 30/60/80% simulated hits. Owner: Redwood infra. Estimated 2 hours.
3) Production-like spike test: ramp to 2x peak QPS with cold-cache; verify graceful degradation and fallback behavior. Owner: CloudApps + Redwood. Estimated 1 hour.

Next steps I propose this week:
- I will share the unit econ workbook (attached) with configurable knobs.
- CloudApps to share a representative prompt set (10–20k tokens) and a sample request trace.
- Schedule a 2-hour joint bench session (we recommend Wed or Thu afternoon PT).

If that looks right, I’ll loop in Product (Marissa) to propose the exact bench config and Rishi to align on commercial options for a short PoC price.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: redwood_unit_econ_v1.xlsx (workbook, cost model), test-config.yaml (bench config stub)

From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@cloudapps.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cloudapps.com
Date: 2026-10-30T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prod inference audit — 1M-token unit economics & planned bench runs

Jonas — appreciate the clean summary. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

1) The per-1M numbers look promising but we need the sensitivity to cache hit rate. Can you publish the same sheet with toggles for 30/60/80% hit? I saw the workbook but wanted a quick view.
2) For the baseline run, we need to validate the exact model binary you plan to use. Production cannot accept AD-hoc weights that change perf significantly. Can you confirm model name and quantization level?
3) Procurement asked for an indicative PoC price (30 days, up to 50M tokens) and OD contract terms. Can you put together a sample quote we can attach to our internal review?

We can provide a 12k message sample prompt set and a short access window for staging. Wed afternoon PT works.

On the cache assumptions: what instrumentation do you provide to validate hit-rate on our side (we need some observable metrics for auditing)?

—Sam
Sam Lee
Head of Platform Engineering | CloudApps Inc
sam.lee@cloudapps.io

Quoted attachments requested: hyperscaler_quote_sample.pdf (we attached an anonymized sample for comparison).

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@cloudapps.io>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-30T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prod inference audit — 1M-token unit economics & planned bench runs

Sam — quick note from Product/Bench team on the configuration and observability surface. Thanks for offering the prompt set — that will be the most important artifact.

Bench config details we recommend (we will commit to these for the joint run):
- Model image: "llamax-33b-rw-v1" (open checkpoint, FP16 runtime). Quantization: kernel-level FP16 with optional 4-bit path for one follow-up test.
- Runtime flags: continuous_batch=true, max_batch_delay=12ms, batch_target=8, kv_cache=true
- Instrumentation: we will stream a bench report with per-token cost breakdown, KV cache hit/miss counters, GPU utilization, and P50/P95/P99 latencies. We will also expose a short tracing payload per request (no PII).

What we will need from CloudApps for the runs:
- Representative prompt set (10–20k messages), with a note on which prompts are user-generated vs system boilerplate so we can model cache hit potential.
- A short staging key for secure ingestion and a pre-warm window for the service.

Suggested owners & timeline:
- Jonas: schedule the bench session (target Wed 2026-11-03 13:00–15:00 PT).
- Marissa: configure benches and provide instrumented report (deliverable within 24 hours after run).
- Rishi: commercial contact for PoC pricing and contract terms.

On commercial guidance: we can offer a 30-day PoC at a capped rate (example: $0.03 per 1k tokens effective cap for the first 50M tokens) while the bench runs are in progress; we need Procurement to sign a short PoC A/N. Pricing is flexible pending usage patterns and cache effectiveness — we will formalize after the bench.

I attached a sample bench YAML (test-config.yaml) and updated cost sheet with toggles for 30/60/80% hits. Jonas — I updated the workbook (see redwood_unit_econ_v1.xlsx).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Product | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: test-config.yaml, redwood_unit_econ_v1.xlsx (updated with toggle), bench-run-report-template.md

- If CloudApps signs by EOD Friday, we will reserve dedicated pool capacity for the bench slot on Wed.

Jonas: please include the DocuSign link in the scheduling thread. Marissa: stand by to finalize bench run configuration once procurement confirms.

Rishi Malhotra
